   234→    /// Verifies a batch of cell-proof-commitment triplets.
   235→    #[instrument(skip_all, level = "debug", fields(cells = cells.len()))]
   236→    pub fn verify_cell_proof_batch(
   237→        &self,
   238→        cells: &[CellRef<'_>],
   239→        kzg_proofs: &[Bytes48],
   240→        indices: Vec<CellIndex>,
   241→        kzg_commitments: &[Bytes48],
   242→    ) -> Result<(), (Option<u64>, Error)> {
   243→        let mut column_groups: HashMap<u64, Vec<(CellRef, Bytes48, Bytes48)>> = HashMap::new();
   244→
   245→        let expected_len = cells.len();
   246→
   247→        // This check is already made in `validate_data_columns`. However we add it here so that ef consensus spec tests pass
   248→        // and to avoid any potential footguns in the future. Note that by catching the error here and not in `validate_data_columns`
   249→        // the error becomes non-attributable.
   250→        if kzg_proofs.len() != expected_len
   251→            || indices.len() != expected_len
   252→            || kzg_commitments.len() != expected_len
   253→        {
   254→            return Err((
   255→                None,
   256→                Error::InconsistentArrayLength("Invalid data column".to_string()),
   257→            ));
   258→        }
   259→
   260→        for (((cell, proof), &index), commitment) in cells
   261→            .iter()
   262→            .zip(kzg_proofs.iter())
   263→            .zip(indices.iter())
   264→            .zip(kzg_commitments.iter())
   265→        {
   266→            column_groups
   267→                .entry(index)
   268→                .or_default()
   269→                .push((cell, *proof, *commitment));
   270→        }
   271→
   272→        let span = Span::current();
   273→        column_groups
   274→            .into_par_iter()
   275→            .map(|(column_index, column_data)| {
   276→                let mut cells = Vec::new();
   277→                let mut proofs = Vec::new();
   278→                let mut commitments = Vec::new();
   279→
   280→                for (cell, proof, commitment) in &column_data {
   281→                    cells.push(*cell);
   282→                    proofs.push(proof.as_ref());
   283→                    commitments.push(commitment.as_ref());
   284→                }
   285→
   286→                // Create per-chunk tracing span for visualizing parallel processing.
   287→                // This is safe from span explosion as we have at most 128 chunks,
   288→                // i.e. the number of column indices.
   289→                let _span = tracing::debug_span!(
   290→                    parent: span.clone(),
   291→                    "verify_cell_proof_chunk",
   292→                    cells = cells.len(),
   293→                    column_index,
   294→                    verification_result = tracing::field::Empty,
   295→                )
   296→                .entered();
   297→
   298→                let verification_result = self.context().verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch(
   299→                    commitments,
   300→                    &vec![column_index; cells.len()], // All column_data here is from the same index
   301→                    cells,
   302→                    proofs,
   303→                );
   304→
   305→                match verification_result {
   306→                    Ok(_) => Ok(()),
   307→                    Err(e) if e.is_proof_invalid() => {
   308→                        Err((Some(column_index), Error::KzgVerificationFailed))
   309→                    }
   310→                    Err(e) => Err((Some(column_index), Error::PeerDASKZG(e))),
   311→                }
   312→            })
   313→            .collect::<Result<Vec<()>, (Option<u64>, Error)>>()?;
   314→
   315→        Ok(())
   316→    }

   319→        &self,

   328→        // Convert the proof type to a c-kzg proof type
   329→        let c_kzg_proof = proofs.map(KzgProof);

    24→/// User-friendly rate limiting parameters of the GCRA.
    25→///
    26→/// A quota of `max_tokens` tokens every `replenish_all_every` units of time means that:
    27→/// 1. One token is replenished every `replenish_all_every`/`max_tokens` units of time.
    28→/// 2. Instantaneous bursts (batches) of up to `max_tokens` tokens are allowed.
    29→///
    30→/// The above implies that if `max_tokens` is greater than 1, the perceived rate may be higher (but
    31→/// bounded) than the defined rate when instantaneous bursts occur. For instance, for a rate of
    32→/// 4T/2s a first burst of 4T is allowed with subsequent requests of 1T every 0.5s forever,
    33→/// producing a perceived rate over the window of the first 2s of 8T. However, subsequent sliding
    34→/// windows of 2s keep the limit.
    35→///
    36→/// In this scenario using the same rate as above, the sender is always maxing out their tokens,
    37→/// except at seconds 1.5, 3, 3.5 and 4
    38→///
    39→/// ```ignore
    40→///            x
    41→///      used  x
    42→///    tokens  x           x           x
    43→///      at a  x  x  x     x  x        x
    44→///     given  +--+--+--o--+--+--o--o--o--> seconds
    45→///      time  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
    46→///            0     1     2     3     4
    47→///
    48→///            4  1  1  1  2  1  1  2  3 <= available tokens when the batch is received
    49→/// ```
    50→///
    51→/// For a sender to request a batch of `n`T, they would need to wait at least
    52→/// n*`replenish_all_every`/`max_tokens` units of time since their last request.
    53→///
    54→/// To produce hard limits, set `max_tokens` to 1.
    55→#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    56→pub struct Quota {
    57→    /// How often are `max_tokens` fully replenished.
    58→    pub(super) replenish_all_every: Duration,
    59→    /// Token limit. This translates on how large can an instantaneous batch of
    60→    /// tokens be.
    61→    pub(super) max_tokens: NonZeroU64,
    62→}
    63→
    64→impl Quota {
    65→    /// A hard limit of one token every `seconds`.
    66→    pub const fn one_every(seconds: u64) -> Self {
    67→        Quota {
    68→            replenish_all_every: Duration::from_secs(seconds),
    69→            max_tokens: NonZeroU64::new(1).unwrap(),
    70→        }
    71→    }
    72→
    73→    /// Allow `n` tokens to be use used every `seconds`.
    74→    pub const fn n_every(n: NonZeroU64, seconds: u64) -> Self {
    75→        Quota {
    76→            replenish_all_every: Duration::from_secs(seconds),
    77→            max_tokens: n,
    78→        }
    79→    }
    80→}

   232→    kzg_commitments: KzgCommitments<E>,
   233→    kzg_commitments_inclusion_proof: FixedVector<Hash256, E::KzgCommitmentsInclusionProofDepth>,
   234→    signed_block_header: SignedBeaconBlockHeader,
   235→    blob_cells_and_proofs_vec: Vec<CellsAndKzgProofs>,
   236→    spec: &ChainSpec,
   237→) -> Result<DataColumnSidecarList<E>, String> {
   238→    let number_of_columns = E::number_of_columns();
   239→    let max_blobs_per_block = spec
   240→        .max_blobs_per_block(signed_block_header.message.slot.epoch(E::slots_per_epoch()))
   241→        as usize;
   242→    let mut columns = vec![Vec::with_capacity(max_blobs_per_block); number_of_columns];
   243→    let mut column_kzg_proofs = vec![Vec::with_capacity(max_blobs_per_block); number_of_columns];
   244→
   245→    for (blob_cells, blob_cell_proofs) in blob_cells_and_proofs_vec {
   246→        // we iterate over each column, and we construct the column from "top to bottom",
   247→        // pushing on the cell and the corresponding proof at each column index. we do this for
   248→        // each blob (i.e. the outer loop).
   249→        for col in 0..number_of_columns {
   250→            let cell = blob_cells
   251→                .get(col)
   252→                .ok_or(format!("Missing blob cell at index {col}"))?;
   253→            let cell: Vec<u8> = cell.to_vec();
   254→            let cell = Cell::<E>::from(cell);
   255→
   256→            let proof = blob_cell_proofs

   258→                .ok_or(format!("Missing blob cell KZG proof at index {col}"))?;
   259→

   261→                .get_mut(col)
   262→                .ok_or(format!("Missing data column at index {col}"))?;
   263→            let column_proofs = column_kzg_proofs
   264→                .get_mut(col)
   265→                .ok_or(format!("Missing data column proofs at index {col}"))?;
   266→
   267→            column.push(cell);
   268→            column_proofs.push(*proof);
   269→        }
   270→    }

   272→    let sidecars: Vec<Arc<DataColumnSidecar<E>>> = columns
   273→        .into_iter()
   274→        .zip(column_kzg_proofs)
   275→        .enumerate()

   281→                kzg_proofs: VariableList::from(proofs),
   282→                signed_block_header: signed_block_header.clone(),
   283→                kzg_commitments_inclusion_proof: kzg_commitments_inclusion_proof.clone(),
   284→            })
   285→        })

55→    /// Returns `Some((effective_epoch, new_cgc))` if the registration results in a CGC update.
    56→    pub(crate) fn register_validators<E: EthSpec>(
    57→        &mut self,
    58→        validators_and_balance: ValidatorsAndBalances,
    59→        current_slot: Slot,
    60→        spec: &ChainSpec,
    61→    ) -> Option<(Epoch, u64)> {
    62→        for (validator_index, effective_balance) in validators_and_balance {
    63→            self.validators
    64→                .insert(validator_index, (current_slot, effective_balance));
    65→        }
    66→
    67→        // Drop validators that haven't re-registered with the node for `VALIDATOR_REGISTRATION_EXPIRY_SLOTS`.
    68→        self.validators
    69→            .retain(|_, (slot, _)| *slot >= current_slot - VALIDATOR_REGISTRATION_EXPIRY_SLOTS);
    70→
    71→        // Each `BALANCE_PER_ADDITIONAL_CUSTODY_GROUP` effectively contributes one unit of "weight".
    72→        let validator_custody_units = self.validators.values().map(|(_, eb)| eb).sum::<u64>()
    73→            / spec.balance_per_additional_custody_group;
    74→        let validator_custody_requirement =
    75→            get_validators_custody_requirement(validator_custody_units, spec);
    76→
    77→        tracing::debug!(
    78→            validator_custody_units,
    79→            validator_custody_requirement,
    80→            "Registered validators"
    81→        );
    82→
    83→        // If registering the new validator increased the total validator "units", then
    84→        // add a new entry for the current epoch
    85→        if Some(validator_custody_requirement) > self.latest_validator_custody_requirement() {
    86→            // Apply the change from the next epoch after adding some delay buffer to ensure
    87→            // the node has enough time to subscribe to subnets etc, and to avoid having
    88→            // inconsistent column counts within an epoch.
    89→            let effective_delay_slots =
    90→                CUSTODY_CHANGE_DA_EFFECTIVE_DELAY_SECONDS / spec.seconds_per_slot;
    91→            let effective_epoch =
    92→                (current_slot + effective_delay_slots).epoch(E::slots_per_epoch()) + 1;
    93→            self.epoch_validator_custody_requirements
    94→                .entry(effective_epoch)
    95→                .and_modify(|old_custody| *old_custody = validator_custody_requirement)
    96→                .or_insert(validator_custody_requirement);
    97→            Some((effective_epoch, validator_custody_requirement))
    98→        } else {
    99→            None
   100→        }
